summary: Ch.0 (prologue): one day a nameless man claiming to be a superior demon appears before the halfling demon Jaekyung, calls him his property and takes over his home. Jaekyung starts dreaming of him (dream scene left untranslated), wakes up shocked, and cannot stop thinking about it. Teaser: a superior demon and a halfling fox start living together.

Ch.1: After a flash-forward of the demon's offer ('take my seed'), Jaekyung's empty restaurant gets a strange customer: a gorgeous, tackily dressed man who demands 'what is rightfully mine'. Jaekyung takes him for a robber and threatens him with a knife; the man knocks it away with sheer power, Jaekyung's fox form slips out and he begs forgiveness from a demon far above his league, who calls him his property and demands he hand 'it' over.

The demon follows Jaekyung home while keeping hold of him, and Jaekyung realizes too late that his home's barrier could have helped him escape. Jaekyung learns that the visitor knows Sahyun and wants to reclaim something entrusted to him, but Sahyun is sleeping elsewhere and the demon refuses to wait for him to wake. Wonyoung finally appears and explains that the visitor is his original master, so he cannot drive him away. Jaekyung mistakes their bond for a secret sexual relationship and launches into frantic accusations. The demon angrily silences him, leaving Jaekyung fearing for his life and wishing the whole ordeal were a dream.

Ch.3: Jaekyung recalls being an abandoned halfling child taken in by Sahyun, and how Wonyoung, once a sword in the house, became a black cluster, a cat and finally a man. The demon reveals that the 'thing' he left there is Wonyoung himself; Jaekyung protests he cannot live without him, and the newly woken, irritable demon silences him. Wonyoung shows the demon modern things -- a smart speaker, the TV, an air conditioner -- and Jaekyung, finding courage, tells him his outfit is tacky.

Ch.4: Stung at being called tacky, the demon -- always proud of his fashion through every era -- decides to go shopping, and Wonyoung takes Jaekyung's wallet to pay. Restyled head to toe the demon is so handsome that shoppers take him for a model, while he wonders why prickly Sahyun kept a halfling like Jaekyung around. When the demon moves on to shoes, Jaekyung's phone shows his account already overdrawn and he drags them home.

Ch.5: Broke after the shopping trip, Jaekyung grudgingly cooks dinner, and the demon complains about the small portions. When the demon refuses to give his name, Jaekyung dubs him 'Kim Anon' and stands his ground despite his terrifying aura, then begs him not to take Wonyoung when he leaves. The demon decides to stay and rest at the house since Sahyun is gone, remarking that Wonyoung has become quite human.

Ch.6: Jaekyung dreams of the demon, half-dressed and teasing, and the dream turns sexual. He wakes horrified to find he had a wet dream about 'Mr. Anon' at thirty years old and washes his clothes in secret, but the demon catches him, having smelled and heard it from his room, and teases him in front of Wonyoung, leaving Jaekyung utterly humiliated.

Ch.7: Demons live hidden among humans, their true forms visible at night only to other demons and halflings, and they make up most of the customers at Jaekyung's midnight restaurant Slacker's. Jaekyung haggles for huge-eyed crabs with frog-demon fishmonger Mr. Hwang while still mortified by his dream. At home he shares the leftover crab with Wonyoung, asks the demon how long he will stay ('I don't know'), and sees Wonyoung collapse from exhaustion after five days of being bossed around -- but dares not object for fear the demon will leave and take Wonyoung.

Ch.8: The demon visits a cafe run by an old demon acquaintance who deals in favors. Using Jaekyung's card, he gets an Americano and a smartphone, declines an offer to pay 'with his essence', and instead sells a superb red gem for cash, with ID and a passport promised for the next day. He muses that he feels oddly content despite his lack of desire. Back at the house, someone rings the doorbell.

Ch.9: The broker demon from the cafe, carrying a red parasol, waits outside the house since he cannot cross Sahyun's barrier without permission; Jaekyung hides, finding him beautiful but frightening. He chats with Wonyoung, amazed that he was once the sword. The demon returns and receives a bag of goods; the broker asks to have 'that halfling' and is told Jaekyung belongs to Sahyun. Jaekyung then asks if the broker is the demon's gigolo, gets flicked for his filthy mind and sent to fetch food, grumbling that the two are equally mysterious and scary.

Ch.10: The demon eats huge amounts of Jaekyung's cooking, saying the food suits him, which flusters Jaekyung. He goes out again; later Jaekyung finds him wearing Jaekyung's prized imported sneakers, refusing the old pair left for him. A new smartphone rings: the demon bought it with Jaekyung's card, then hands him five million won in cash and leaves to open a bank account. Jaekyung celebrates before realising he only got his own money back.

Ch.11: Jaekyung asks Wonyoung who Mr. Anon really is; Wonyoung cannot say, bound to his master. Jaekyung begs him not to leave if the demon takes him, calling him family, and wants to ask the demon to nullify Wonyoung's contract. The demon returns with shopping bags and Jaekyung rescues his sneakers. At dinner the demon notes that powerful demons can only be sated by other demons' blood or energy, yet Jaekyung's cooking fills him as if he were eating another demon.

Ch.12: The demon finds famous-cafe food bland, while Jaekyung's home cooking delights him. Jaekyung, fuming at being lorded over, goes to bed and dreams again of the demon, this time in his restaurant's kitchen wearing only an apron; the dream turns sexual despite his protests (scene left untranslated).

Ch.13: Jaekyung wakes aroused from another dream of Mr. Anon and relieves himself, discovering he wants something inside him as in the dream; afterwards he panics, wondering if he has fallen for the demon. At breakfast he flees to work blushing; Wonyoung wonders why he is acting strange while the demon smirks that the boy is young and weak.

Ch.14: At Slacker's a human regular says Jaekyung is glowing and asks if he is dating; a crocodile-demon regular complains she scares him, and Jaekyung toys with making the place human-only. Customers keep saying he looks lively. The demon texts him to buy beer; Jaekyung dreams of getting stronger or richer and fleeing overseas with Wonyoung, but Wonyoung says only the demon can nullify his contract, and Jaekyung belongs to Sahyun. At home the demon has bought a new sofa with his own money, rubs Jaekyung's fox ears, calls him puppy-like and cute, and orders him to make a snack for the beer.

Ch.15: Jaekyung retaliates by serving the demon a plain breakfast; the demon demands Western or Chinese food and shows him food photos. Jaekyung complains about cooking every day and the packages the demon orders daily; the demon unboxes clothes, and Jaekyung fumes that it is unfair while he works and cleans. The demon orders the wrong shoes, the latest design from an expensive brand, and gives them to Jaekyung, who is overjoyed, calls him Mr. Anon and offers to cook whatever he likes. The demon muses that the halfling's power is negligible yet he never fears him, finds him pathetic and adorable, and flicks him away when he gets too excited.

Ch.16: Jaekyung dreams again of a gentle Mr. Anon in a suit, knows it is a dream, and decides he can do whatever he wants; he undresses him, is shocked by his size, and asks him to take him. He wakes wet as in the dream and thinks that if the real Mr. Anon were half as nice he might tolerate him, but the demon only orders tea. The demon notes it is rare even for halflings to be affected so deeply by his influence.

Ch.17: Jaekyung finds the shoe cabinet crammed with the demon's shoes; the demon mocks the idea that he has friends. He meets his childhood friend Hyunseok, a horse demon who runs a farm back home, who gives him strawberries and warns that a ruthless, dangerous demon who used to work in China has recently moved into the area. The demon turns up nearby claiming he came out for a new convenience-store item, follows Jaekyung, and eyes the strawberries.

Ch.18: Over Hyunseok's strawberries the demon says horse demons are notoriously hard to befriend. Jaekyung recalls his childhood in Sahyun's village beside a horse-demon clan: the horse-demon kids shunned him as a halfling, Sahyun told him people dislike those who are different and that he is not his dad, just Sahyun. Lonely, Jaekyung wished hard for a friend, and something strange appeared out of nowhere: that was the first time he met Wonyoung.

Ch.19: Jaekyung tells how Wonyoung grew from a blob to a cat to a talking boy with Sahyun's face, his true form the sword in storage; with a guardian and a friend he was happy, and in high school he cleared Hyunseok of a theft accusation and won the horse demons over. The demon only half listens and leaves; recalling Hyunseok's rumour, Jaekyung decides the dangerous demon must be Mr. Anon and panics, then concludes the demon just stays home bossing him around and bingeing K-dramas with late-night delivery.

Ch.20: Hyunseok comes back to eat at Slacker's; Jaekyung admits one of Sahyun's clients is living with him. Hyunseok warns him that any client of Sahyun is no ordinary demon and that a great demon, one of the top ten in raw power, has been reported in the area on Demon Network; customers gossip about the photo. Jaekyung recalls how Sahyun moved to the city for him and gave him the mark that protects him, reassures himself, and opens the Demon Network post to see the great demon for himself.

Ch.21: Jaekyung reassures himself that as a member of Sahyun's household under his barrier, the great demon cannot kill him. At home the demon and Wonyoung feast on pizza and beer every night. Jaekyung shows the demon his photo on Demon Network, where he is called the great demon 'L'; the demon is unbothered, refuses to give his name and leaves the cleaning to others. He says he is about 2,000 years old and mellowed out after his destructive youth; Jaekyung is glad he met him this millennium. A TV ad for a waterpark makes the demon order everyone to go the next day, where he shows off in swim trunks.

Ch.22: Jaekyung recalls envying classmates' family trips, since Sahyun refused amusement parks and pools. At the waterpark the demon is giddy as a child and drags Jaekyung onto rides while Wonyoung waits on a sunbed; Jaekyung has fun despite himself and is flustered by the demon's bare skin. Over his homemade kimbap the demon demands a java chip frappe; going for coffee, Jaekyung bumps into a stranger.

Ch.23: At the waterpark a now middle-aged college friend recognises Jaekyung but decides he cannot be the same person; Jaekyung explains to himself that halflings age slowly and lose touch with humans. The demon, who bought only his own frappe, mocks the idea of a halfling marrying; Jaekyung says he might meet a fellow halfling through a demon marriage agency, though since the dream he wonders if he likes men too. The demon drags him to the wave pool, finds it dull, and fusses over him when he gets knocked over.

Ch.24: Jaekyung comforts a lost boy, Woojin, and returns him to his mother; the demon thinks he would make a good parent. The demon asks Wonyoung whether Sahyun gave him human form for the halfling's sake; Wonyoung says it was Jaekyung who changed him. After ice cream they drive home and the demon confronts Jaekyung, who has almost no demonic energy; Wonyoung insists Jaekyung awakened him, Jaekyung refuses to believe it, and the demon wonders what Sahyun has hidden.

Ch.25: After Jaekyung's rough driving the demon signs up for driving lessons, aces the tests and shops for cars; he mocks Jaekyung for logging expenses by hand and not knowing app perks or Grape Pay, and boasts of asset managers in Hong Kong. Bored, he considers moving somewhere new; Jaekyung asks him to leave Wonyoung behind since Wonyoung is family, recalling that Wonyoung was his only friend and Sahyun will sleep another decade. The demon calls Wonyoung his weapon and the transformation theft; Jaekyung protests it was not on purpose, and the demon concludes he is too simple to scheme, then tells him that if he hates being weak he need only kill other demons.

Ch.26: Jaekyung refuses to kill demons to grow stronger. The demon reflects that he gained power by killing for millennia, which let something possess Wonyoung, so he left Wonyoung with Sahyun, who absorbed the karma to stave off the illness of a demon that does not kill. Learning it was the halfling who awakened Wonyoung, the demon decides he must pay: too weak to eat, Jaekyung will instead bear the demon's clone so he can absorb it and recover. He orders Jaekyung to take his clothes off.

Ch.27: The demon forces himself on Jaekyung despite his protests (scene left untranslated). Afterwards Jaekyung, in tears, asks how he could do this; the demon remarks that he is surprised Jaekyung did not change form through it all.

Ray reveals that his apparent threat to eat his own child was a test to make Jaekyung transform or unleash hidden powers, leaving Jaekyung frightened and furious. Ray remains curious about how Jaekyung transformed Wonyoung and wonders whether Sahyun’s awakening will provide answers. Jaekyung then discovers that his restaurant has been destroyed, apparently by someone searching for Ray, the great demon staying at his home as Sahyun’s guest. When Hyunseok realizes who the guest is, he scolds Jaekyung for being reckless and insists he stay with him, but Jaekyung feels unfairly blamed and leaves. While driving home, Jaekyung is attacked by high-level demons who identify him as the halfling seen with Ray, drag him from his car, and demand Ray’s whereabouts. The chapter ends with Jaekyung crying out for help.

Ray, known as the Great Demon, kills attackers seeking to avenge their lord, reducing them to dust. His companion, an unnamed shopkeeper, is horrified after witnessing death for the first time, and Ray drives the shopkeeper home. During the ride, the shopkeeper reveals that the attackers wrecked the shop and scrawled Ray's name everywhere while searching for him. Ray insists on being called 'Ray' instead of 'Mr. Anon,' explaining that it is not his true name but one he has been known by for 1,000 years, and they bicker over whether it suits him. When they arrive home and find more enemies, the frightened shopkeeper begs Ray not to kill them. Ray then calls someone and demands a house he can live in immediately.

Ray takes his halfling companion to a luxurious temporary apartment arranged by an acquaintance, who recognizes the halfling from Sahyun’s house and remarks that Ray has changed before leaving. Wonyoung reports that Ray’s enemies are camping outside his house and taking shifts demanding his appearance, so Ray instructs Wonyoung to come to the new address without being followed. Ray plans to scatter his scent in various places to divert his pursuers. He sends the trembling halfling to take a warm shower, while the halfling privately reflects on being terrified after witnessing powerful demons turn to dust in an instant. The chapter ends with Ray checking on the halfling in the bath and saying he thought the halfling had drowned.

A great demon interrupts a halfling’s bath, ignores the halfling’s protests, and discovers that the halfling’s demonic power is exhausted. Admitting responsibility, the demon offers to share his power, astonishing the halfling because powerful demons rarely give strength to outsiders and even Sahyun has never shared his. The halfling expects a power crystal, but the demon instead transfers power through a forceful kiss and continues unwanted intimate touching. The demon becomes angry upon discovering that the halfling has absorbed almost none of the power and questions Sahyun’s teaching. The chapter ends with the halfling tearfully explaining that Sahyun taught reading, writing, and transformation spells, but never shared power, leaving the halfling unsure how to receive it.
